title: Theming
lead: A theme style is the whole look of the components. On top of it go dark mode, a colour theme, a density and your own overrides, all without touching component code.

styles.title: Theme styles
styles.p1: Four theme styles ship in `@skeinui/themes`. Each covers every component, in light and dark:
styles.name: Style
styles.default: Skein's own: brand blue, larger radius, subtle shadows.
styles.heroui: HeroUI v3: soft colours, pill-shaped controls.
styles.p2: Import the CSS of the ones you use; only those are bundled. Several can be imported together, each scoped by `data-theme-style`, so users can switch between them at runtime (the admin template's preferences drawer does that).

mode.title: Light and dark
mode.p1: `mode` is `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"` (follows the OS and updates when it changes). Every theme style has both palettes; nothing else to import.

colors.title: Colour themes and density
colors.p1: Colour themes change only colours and work on top of any theme style: `purple`, `green`, `geekblue`, `volcano`, and `contrast` (WCAG AA). The compact density makes controls smaller.

overrides.title: Your own values
overrides.p1: For a brand colour, a radius or a density of your own, `themeOverrides` sets them on top of the theme style. Colours are `#rrggbb`; `dark` overrides them in dark mode; radius is in rem; density is a multiplier (1 = default).

own-style.title: A theme style of your own
own-style.p1: When overrides aren't enough, write a theme style. The CLI copies a bundled one into `src/theme/` under a new name, so you start from something complete and change what you want:
own-style.p2: `skein theme check` compares it with the components' contract and lists every slot, variant and state it doesn't style yet. Without `--from` you get a blank style to fill.

how.title: How it works
how.p1: Components write `data-*` attributes and no CSS; a theme style is CSS that targets them, scoped by `data-theme-style`:
how.p2: Tokens (`--ui-c-primary`, `--ui-radius`, `--ui-density`…) are defined per style in `tokens.css` and `dark.css`; colour themes and `themeOverrides` only change token values, which is why they work with any style.
